turns.question: Our DO calibration is done in air rather than in a solution. What does the SOP actually require for the setup, and how do we tell it worked?
turns.answer:
The SOP's DO calibration uses a water-saturated air environment, not a liquid standard. Setup: place a wet sponge or wet paper towel in the bottom of the calibration container, put the DO probe in loosely fitted so moisture can't escape while ambient pressure is maintained, and keep the probe and temperature sensor from touching the wet items 【1†"Create a 100 percent water-saturated air environment by placing a wet sponge or a wet paper towel on the bottom of the DO calibration container"】. Let the confined air become saturated (about 10 to 15 minutes), with the instrument on to warm up the probe, and make sure temperature readings stabilize before continuing 【1†"Allow the confined air to become saturated with water vapor (saturation occurs in approximately 10 to 15 minutes)"】.

Then, in calibration mode, select "DO %" and enter the local barometric pressure measured on-site — not from weather services unless corrected for elevation 【2†"Enter the local barometric pressure (usually in mm of mercury) for the sampling location into the instrument"】.

How to tell it worked:
- After calibration, switch to measurement mode, set the display to DO mg/L and temperature, and compare against the Oxygen Solubility at Indicated Pressure chart; they should agree within the instrument's accuracy (usually ± 0.2 mg/L), otherwise repeat calibration 【2†"Compare the DO mg/L reading to the Oxygen Solubility at Indicated Pressure chart attached to the SOP"】.
- As a check, place the probe in a 0.0 mg/L DO solution; after readings stabilize, the instrument should read less than 0.5 mg/L (assuming ± 0.2 mg/L accuracy) 【2†"The instrument should read less than 0.5 mg/L (assuming an accuracy of + 0.2 mg/L)"】.

5.3. DISSOLVED OXYGEN

_Dissolved oxygen (DO) content in water is measured using a membrane electrode. To insure
proper operation, the DO probe’s membrane and electrolyte should be replaced prior to
calibration for the sampling event. The new membrane may need to be conditioned before it is
used; consult manufacturer’s manual on how the conditioning is to be performed. Failure to
‘perform this step may lead to erratic measurements. Before performing the
calibration/measurements, inspect the membrane for air bubbles and nicks.

Note: some manufacturers require an altitude correction instead of a barometric correction. In

that case, enter the altitude correction according to the manufacturer’s directions in Step 5 and
then proceed to Step 6. .

Note: | some instruments have a built-in barometer. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for
entering the barometric value in step 5.

Calibration Procedure

1. Gently dry the temperature sensor and remove any water droplets from the DO
probe’s sensor membrane according to manufacturer's instructions. Note that the

evaporation of moisture on the temperature sensor or DO probe may influence the
readings during calibration.

2. Create a 100 percent water-saturated air environment by placing a wet sponge or a

10. After the calibration has been completed, rinse the probe with tap or deionized water
and store the probe according to manufacturer’s instructions. It is important that all of

of environmental samples. |

11. Record calibration information on Table 1.

Note: You can either purchase the 0.0 mg/L DO solution from a vendor or prepare the
solution yourself. To prepare a 0.0 mg/L DO solution, follow the procedure stated in
Standard Methods (Method 4500-O G). The method basically states to add excess
sodium sulfite (until no more dissolves) and a trace amount of cobalt chloride (read
warning on the label before use) to water. This solution is prepared prior to the sampling
event. ‘Note: this solution can be made without cobalt chloride, but the probe will take

_ longer to respond to the low DO concentration.

SPECIFIC CONDUCTANCE

Conductivity is used to measure the ability of an aqueous solution to carry an electrical current.
Specific conductance is the conductivity value corrected to 25°C.

turns.question: We also carry a zero-oxygen solution. What should the meter read in it, and what does it mean if it doesn't?
turns.answer:
In the 0.0 mg/L DO solution, after the readings have stabilized the instrument should read less than 0.5 mg/L (assuming an accuracy of ± 0.2 mg/L) 【2†"The instrument should read less than 0.5 mg/L (assuming an accuracy of + 0.2 mg/L)"】.

If it doesn't — specifically, if it reads above 0.5 mg/L or reads negative — the SOP says it will be necessary to clean the probe, and change the membrane and electrolyte solution 【2†"it will be necessary to clean the probe, and change the membrane and electrolyte solution"】. If that doesn't work, try a new 0.0 mg/L DO solution, and if those changes don't work, contact the manufacturer 【2†"If this does not work, try a new 0.0 mg/L DO solution"】.

Note the SOP also cautions that some projects and instruments may have different accuracy requirements, so the 0.5 mg/L value may need adjusting based on those requirements 【2†"Note: some projects and instruments may have different accuracy requirements"】.
